catalog_quote: Phonemically, Nehan word stress is predominately penultimate, occurring on the next to last syllable of the word as in examples (9), (10), and (11). Phonetically, these words show no final vowels. Phonemically, all words in Nehan end in vowels, many of which are dropped in a process called apocope. ... Some words have phonemically assigned final stress and do not lose the final vowel, in which case the stress remains as in examples (12), (13), and (14). (9) /maˈnasa/ 'now' [mɑ.ˈnɑs] (10) /ˈmate/ 'die' [mɑt] (11) /taˈbila/ 'sit' [tɑ.ˈbil] (12) /ingˈga/ '2SG' [iŋ.ˈgɑ] (13) /hiˈre/ 'tell' [hi.ˈrɛ] (14) /liˈuo/ 'morning' [li.ˈwɔ] ... Note that for the phonemic form in numbers 1-11 above the stress is on the penultimate syllable. new_statements.relation_note: The catalog lists Nehan with an empty rule and existing_statements is empty, so this is the first stress statement on record for the language: fixed final stress, from the same SIL team (the Glennons) that wrote the two unopened manuscripts. It fills the empty catalog rule rather than contradicting anything.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of every word, without exception stated; no tone or length contrast is given under the suprasegmentals heading.
new_statements.exceptions: none mentioned ('always'); the OPD adds that consonant-final words have an underlying stem-final vowel that surfaces before clitics, which could bear on the stress domain but the OPD does not say so
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes Nehan (Nissan) [NSN] as spoken at Kalil, Nissan Island, North Solomons Province (major villages Balil, Lihon, Mapiri; population 6000 in 1990). The 2001 manuscript is likewise about 'the Nehan Language of Nissan Island'. No dialect is singled out.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation and locator are confirmed verbatim in the Glennon 2014 text we hold layer (lines 709-720, 784-789) and on a page scan of p. 24 (printed p. the OPD 2009 'Stress is on the last syllable' line and Todd 1978's silence are also re-confirmed in copies we hold. (2) Deciding source: a 2014 MA thesis (syntax) by the long-term SIL fieldworker, with a short but explicit, IPA-exemplified stress statement; Glottolog's entire descriptive bibliography (2 items) is held, and searches of SIL archives (the Internet Archive), OLAC, the SMG NW-Solomonic bibliography and the open web turned up no instrumental, JIPA, or dedicated prosodic study. Newly downloaded: the 2003 OPD (SIL 42419) says 'Stress is always on the last syllable' -- the same surface citation-form statement the record already carries and reconciles via apocope

sources.quote: No stress statement anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult: only English glosses). Headword practice corroborates the thesis's two classes: apocopating words are entered in surface form with the underlying vowel-final form in '(from: ...)', while the thesis's final-stressed items (kale, hire, liuo, inggo, ingga) are entered vowel-final with no alternant.
